\textbf{Source.} Tadelis (2013), \emph{Game Theory: An Introduction}, Exercise 13.9 ``Private Value Linear Bidding'', p.~287 {[}PDF p.~306{]}. Reproduced verbatim. \textbf{Answer in the source:} no (none in the book; Princeton UP's website has about half, not checked).

\begin{quote}
\textbf{Private Value Linear Bidding:} Two players participate in a first-price sealed-bid auction in an IPV setting. The value of the good for each player is given by \(0.5 + \theta_i\), where \(\theta_i\) is observed only by player \(i\) and is uniformly distributed over the interval \([0, 1]\).

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\alph{enumi}.}
\item
  Show that there is a symmetric Bayesian Nash equilibrium in which each bidder \(i\)'s bidding strategy is of the form \(s_i^*(\theta_i) = a + b\theta_i\).
\item
  What is the expected payoff of a player if his type is \(\theta_i\)?
\end{enumerate}
\end{quote}
